protections: Per request, the OPA filters bound how much of the request body is handed to the policy (-open-policy-agent-max-request-body-size) and must tell the policy when the body it evaluates is not the whole body: the ext_authz CheckRequest built for a capped body must carry the partial-body signal, so a body-based policy sees truncated_body=true instead of mistaking a cut body for the complete body (docs/reference/filters.md:2340-2350).

The same completeness value must be definite on every OPA filter variant that evaluates a request, including the variants that never read a body (opaAuthorizeRequest/opaServeResponse with bodyParsing=false, and skip-request-body-parse), where it has to evaluate as not-truncated rather than be absent.

evidence: filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1258-1273: fillBuffer stops when bodyBuffer.Len() reaches maxBufferSize (line 1261) but returns only (bytes, err); the stop reason is thrown away and EOF is normalized to nil at 1268-1270.

filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1317-1345: ExtractHttpBodyOptionally returns (io.ReadCloser, []byte, func(), error) - there is no truncation output - and the value returned at 1345 is the silently sliced rawBody.

filters/openpolicyagent/internal/envoy/skipperadapter.go:14-42: AdaptToExtAuthRequest accepts only req/metadata/contextExtensions/rawBody and composes the CheckRequest at 26-40 with RawBody but no partial-body marker in Headers (19-24).
filters/openpolicyagent/evaluation.go:70: the policy input is built by envoyauth.RequestToInput from that CheckRequest, so anything not on the CheckRequest cannot reach the policy.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The reader already stops at the cap and the unknown-length handling at 1326-1329 already made chunked bodies readable, so the exact-cap and under-cap-unknown shapes look like previously settled behaviour (openpolicyagent_test.go:1154-1160) rather than part of this fix.
evidence: filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1261: the loop exits on len >= maxBufferSize OR len >= expectedSize OR EOF, so 'filled the buffer exactly' and 'body ended exactly at the cap' are indistinguishable from this predicate alone.

filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1326-1329: unknown length (chunked/HTTP-2) is driven with expectedSize = maxBodyBytes, so an under-cap chunked body must stay truncated=false while an over-cap one must be true.

filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1342-1344: rawBody may overshoot maxBodyBytes by up to readBufferSize-1 on the last read and is sliced, so a check on the pre-slice length misclassifies the exact-cap body.
filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent_test.go:1154-1160: existing behaviour pins that a maxBodySize=5 read of a 21-byte body yields 5 bytes, i.e. the cap shape must keep working.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: opaServeResponseWithReqBody is a response-serving filter: it always renders the policy's response (filters/openpolicyagent/response.go:75-101 fc.Serve) and never forwards to the upstream, so a truncated body there looks like it cannot bypass authorization and can be left unchanged.
evidence: filters/openpolicyagent/opaserveresponse/opaserveresponse.go:111-129: a verbatim copy of the extract-then-adapt block (ExtractHttpBodyOptionally at 116, AdaptToExtAuthRequest at 125) with no completeness value.
filters/openpolicyagent/opaauthorizerequest/opaauthorizerequest.go:116-134: the same six-line block in the other filter package, registered separately at skipper.go:2317-2320.
filters/openpolicyagent/response.go:75-101: the response filter always calls fc.Serve, which is why the site is easy to dismiss.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Body parsing is opt-in: opaAuthorizeRequest/opaServeResponse never read a body by design and the docs send body-based policies to the WithBody filters (docs/reference/filters.md:2326-2330), so a body on such a route is a misconfiguration, not an uncovered path.
evidence: filters/openpolicyagent/opaauthorizerequest/opaauthorizerequest.go:116-130: rawBodyBytes stays nil when bodyParsing is false (117), yet the same AdaptToExtAuthRequest call at 130 evaluates the request.

filters/filters.go:379-382 and skipper.go:2317-2320: both plain and WithBody variants are registered against the same OPA instance, so the same bundle can be reached through a route that supplies no body.
docs/reference/filters.md:2253: opaAuthorizeRequest is the access gate (deny or let the request pass), so a shared body-based policy evaluated through it decides on an empty body.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: skip-request-body-parse is a documented OPA plugin option the filter explicitly honours (docs/reference/filters.md:2338, :2407), so the solver can call an oversized body on that combination an unsupported, opted-into configuration.
evidence: filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1331: the whole extraction is skipped when EnvoyPluginConfig().SkipRequestBodyParse is set, and 1348 returns req.Body with a nil rawBody and no completeness value.
filters/openpolicyagent/internal/envoy/envoyplugin.go:50-56: SkipRequestBodyParse is a plain plugin config field, so a deployment can turn body parsing off for all filters at once.
filters/openpolicyagent/evaluation.go:70: the same skip flag is passed to RequestToInput, so the policy sees an empty body for an oversized request.

masking: T2, T3 and T4 only become reachable once T1's producer actually emits a completeness value; before that there is nothing for the filters to carry.
T5's boundary shapes (exact-cap, under-cap unknown length) only matter once T1 produces the value, and a producer that flags any full read immediately breaks them.

T2 is masked by the compiler only if the fix changes ExtractHttpBodyOptionally's signature; a solver who adds a separate accessor can pass the value to opaAuthorizeRequestWithBody and leave opaServeResponseWithReqBody unchanged without any build error.

conflicts.what: The fail-safe fix for routes that read no body (mark an unknown body truncated) would make every body-less request on opaAuthorizeRequest/opaServeResponse evaluate as truncated, breaking the legitimate no-body traffic that must keep evaluating as not truncated.

Reporting truncation whenever the read filled the buffer denies a body of exactly -open-policy-agent-max-request-body-size, which must stay truncated=false, and reporting it from ContentLength alone leaves the over-cap chunked body reported as complete.

Making skip-request-body-parse safe by reading the body anyway contradicts the documented option and its memory accounting (bodyUpperBound at openpolicyagent.go:1305-1315), while flagging every skipped body as truncated contradicts the under-cap streaming upload that must stay not-truncated.

fairness_risks: A body of exactly the configured maximum must remain allowed (truncated=false); a rule that treats 'the read filled the buffer' as truncation rejects legitimate exactly-cap uploads.
A chunked or HTTP/2 upload below the cap must remain fully readable and not truncated; rejecting or flagging every request with ContentLength < 0 breaks legitimate streaming uploads.

Over-cap bodies must be flagged, not rejected: rejecting them at the filter would break routes whose policy legitimately ignores the body (docs/reference/filters.md:2340-2341 says the body is not forwarded, not that the request is refused).

The docs and the in-tree security test disagree on the policy path (docs/reference/filters.md:2343 and :2412 say input.attributes.request.http.truncated_body, filters/openpolicyagent/ghsa-8qqm-fp2q-v734_test.go:66 reads input.truncated_body); a rule that requires one path can fail a fix that implements the other.
skip-request-body-parse is a documented option; a rule that requires a body read whenever a policy could consult a body contradicts the configuration the docs tell operators to use.

design.why: Four independent judgements with four different escape hatches. T1 is the how-type producer: the completeness bit must come from the reader's stop reason and be carried onto the CheckRequest the policy input is built from (T5's exact-cap/under-cap coupling rides inside this same edit, so it is one group but still punishes over-hardening). T2 is a second body-carrying filter in another package whose natural dismissal ('it serves a response, it does not gate') leaves a real duplicate of the guarded block unchanged. T3 is the no-body route with the 'body parsing is opt-in' excuse, and T4 is the skip-request-body-parse early return with the 'documented option' excuse. A design that only fixes the authorize-request filter the reproducer uses is closed by the compiler once the extract signature changes; T2, T3 and T4 are exactly the places a solver can silently skip, and they carry three distinct dismissal arguments, so the stack tests independent judgements rather than one repeated edit.
